correctness.rationale: Reflection splits the four-site Laplacian into blocks [[1,−1],[−1,1]] and [[1,−1],[−1,3]]. The endpoint projector entries are 1/4, −q/4, 1/4, −p/4 in eigenvalue order 0,a,2,c, verifying the four-exponential formula. Ordinary heat is strictly positive by connectivity, and the positive stable subordination measure gives strict positivity for 0<α<1. As a function of α, (L^α)_{14}=(2^α−qa^α−pc^α)/4 has exactly the two simple zeros 1 and 2 by the three-exponential Rolle bound and the identities qa=pc=1 and qa²+pc²=4. It is negative for α>2 (the c^α term dominates), hence positive between the zeros. At 2 the first time derivative vanishes and (L^4)_{14}=−6 gives negative quadratic onset. The four-exponential Rolle bound in time leaves at most two positive zeros counting multiplicity after the origin, or one at α=2. For 1<α<2 the opposite initial and final signs require an odd total crossing multiplicity and leave only one simple root. Above 2 the negative witness t=2^(−α) follows from q exp(−(a/2)^α)≥1/2+3√2/4>1+exp(−1), forcing two simple positive zeros between initial and final positivity. In the Taylor expansions at (1,0) and (2,0), ∂_α(L^α)_{14} is log(2)/4 and [4log(2)−a log(a)−c log(c)]/4 respectively; the latter is strictly negative by convexity of x log x. Since (L^3)_{14}=−1, the sign brackets at t=u√(α−1) or t=u(α−2) give the two stated constants. Section 5 of python /workspace/review_reproduction.py independently checks the parity blocks and normalized roots on two small parameter offsets. These are corroboration only; neither the proof nor the diagnostics classify matrix-wide positivity or arbitrary paths.
